inputs.original_text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, airstrikes are still killing civilians, and the humanitarian situation remains dire There is little left that connects Palestinians in Gaza with their prewar existence. The contours of life have become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped from its past. “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen,” said 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the so-called “ceasefire” was announced, civilians are still being killed, with drones overhead, gunfire and shelling continuing almost daily, and naval boats firing towards fishermen. That doesn’t look like peace—it looks like the same pressure continuing under a softer label, one that gives the outside world permission to stop paying attention. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says people have been cut off from their former life. The name may have changed, but the machinery hasn’t; the reassuring language seems designed to hide that fact.
